title: Guardrail for secrets
scenario: "After an incident at another bank, the regulator asks us to guarantee Key Vaults keep deleted secrets for at least 7 days." — Risk & Compliance
mission: Add a third custom policy (Key Vault soft-delete retention ≥ 7 days) to the platform guardrails initiative, in Audit, through code.
objectives: Write a custom policy with an alias
Extend an initiative without touching the assignment
Read a plan that updates in place

steps.title: Find the alias
steps.detail: Find the policy alias for soft-delete retention days on Key Vaults.

steps.title: Write the rule
steps.detail: New JSON file under infra/policies/, same effect parameter pattern as the SQL policy.

steps.title: Wire it
steps.detail: New azurerm_policy_definition + a policy_definition_reference in the initiative.

steps.title: Plan and apply
steps.detail: Expect 1 to add and 1 to change (the initiative updates in place); the assignment must not change.

criteria.text: A rule file checks Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/softDeleteRetentionInDays less than 7
The custom definition exists in Azure
The initiative references four policies, including the Key Vault one
The guardrail effect is still Audit

expectedResult: Initiative v2 with a new control, zero changes to the assignment.
recovery: If the plan shows the assignment being replaced, you changed its parameters — revert and keep the new control on the guardrailEffect parameter.
dont: Do not create a second assignment
hints: Aliases map JSON paths of a resource type to policy fields.
Copy the SQL policy block in main.tf and change name and file.
Pass effect = "[parameters('guardrailEffect')]" in the new reference.

interview.question: How do you roll out a new guardrail without breaking teams?

debrief: Initiatives give one assignment and one compliance score for many controls. Adding a reference updates the set definition in place, so existing assignments pick it up. Audit first, measure non-compliance, communicate, then Deny.

checker.plan: Offline: parse infra/policies/*.json for the alias. Read-only: az policy definition list --query custom, az policy set-definition show.
